title: AI Unlocked: Politics & Governance
blurb: For campaigners, public servants, and civic organizations: policy analysis at speed, constituent communication, campaign operations, disinformation defense, and the ethics/regulation landscape shaping AI in public life.

modules.t: AI in Public Life: The Map
modules.d: Where AI is reshaping campaigns, government, and civic space.
modules.body:
Landscape

  • Government: service chatbots, document processing, translation, case triage.
  • Campaigns: micro-drafted communication, voter-file analytics, rapid response.
  • Civic risk: deepfakes, synthetic astroturf, and trust erosion — defense is a core skill here.

This course is rigorously non-partisan: the skills serve any democratic actor; the ethics bind all of them.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres has warned repeatedly of AI deployed "without guardrails", and the EU AI Act — the world’s first comprehensive AI law — now sets the regulatory tone globally. Civic actors who master both the tools and the rules will define the next decade of public life.

modules.d: Summarize, compare, and stress-test policy at speed.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Bill/report summarization with "what changed vs current law" tables.
  • Stakeholder impact mapping; comparative policy scans across countries.
  • Devil's advocate on your own policy memo before opponents do it for you.
  • Long-context tools (AI Studio/Claude) for entire bill texts and hearing transcripts.
plAIbox™: produce a 2-page brief on a live policy issue: summary, three options, costs, risks, and the strongest opposing argument fairly stated.
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as a rigorously non-partisan policy analyst. Summarize this bill/policy [paste or name]: what changes vs current law (table), who is affected and how, three implementation risks, the strongest argument FOR and AGAINST stated fairly, and five questions a journalist should ask its sponsors.

modules.d: Multilingual, accessible, and honest at scale.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Correspondence triage and reply drafting (human sign-off always).
  • Plain-language versions of policies at multiple reading levels and languages.
  • Town-hall prep: anticipated-question banks with sourced answers.
  • Transparency norm: disclose AI assistance in official communication where policy requires.

modules.d: Field, fundraising, and rapid response — within the rules.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Volunteer onboarding kits, walk scripts, and event logistics automated.
  • Fundraising appeals A/B drafted; donor thank-you pipelines.
  • Rapid response: monitored topics → drafted responses → human approval → publish.
  • Rules module: election law on AI disclosures, robocalls, and synthetic media varies by jurisdiction and is tightening — verify before deploying anything voter-facing.

quiz.q: Voter-facing synthetic media should be deployed…
opts: Only after checking jurisdiction rules and with disclosure

modules.d: Detect, inoculate, and respond to synthetic manipulation.
modules.body:
Defense stack

  • Deepfake tells and verification workflows (provenance checks, reverse search, frame analysis).
  • Pre-bunking: inoculation messaging that builds audience immunity.
  • Incident playbook: verify → document → counter-message → report to platforms.
  • Protecting your own likeness and channels.

modules.d: Your organization’s operating rules and running workflows.
modules.body:
Capstone

  • Three live workflows (analysis, communication, response), your jurisdiction's rules memo, a disinformation incident plan, and a public AI-use statement — presented to the panel.
